headline: Law extends federal missing and exploited children programs through 2028 and expands duties of the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children.
what_it_does: The law renews federal programs for missing and exploited children through fiscal year 2028. It replaces the legal term "child pornography" with "child sexual abuse material" in the Missing Children's Assistance Act. It gives the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) clear legal authority to help get child sexual abuse material removed from the internet, and lets it offer recovery support such as counseling recommendations. It also requires NCMEC to report more information each year, including data on children missing from state-sponsored care.

who_it_affects.group: Missing and sexually exploited children and their families
who_it_affects.how: NCMEC may provide them support services and recovery help, including counseling recommendations and community support.

who_it_affects.group: Victims depicted in child sexual abuse material online
who_it_affects.how: NCMEC now has formal legal authority to help handle requests to remove such content from the internet.

who_it_affects.group: Children in foster care or other state-sponsored care
who_it_affects.how: NCMEC's public annual report must count how many go missing, how many are recovered, and how many are likely victims of child sex trafficking.
NCMEC must report yearly on how it chooses forensic partners and recommends forensic resources to police.
They can receive consultation and assistance from NCMEC on recovery support for children.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted June 17, 2024; programs are reauthorized through fiscal year 2028.
